references.text: A direct narrative continuation confirming that the father's life is existentially dependent on the boy.
Concretizes the consequence from the source verse by depicting the father's death and the depth of grief.
Reveals the personal burden of guilt and the intermediary role underlying the fear of the father's death.
Formulates the same theological insight as an impossible question about the fatal consequences of separation.
Creates a theological contrast between relational dependence (Genesis) and individual responsibility for sin (Ezekiel).
